reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode, data through Nov 6 and not stale: SPX -5.96% from its 120-day high, -3.94% below its 50-day but +0.71% above its 200-day; SMH -30.94% from its high and below Zone 2 ($470-505) while NVDA sits between zones at $186.64; VIX 25.64 rolling over from a 28.18 five-day high, HY OAS 3.48 calm, mechanical tally 3 of 4 with zone occupancy the missing leg.
reaction.invalidation: Two consecutive closes with SMH inside Zone 2, VIX below 25 and the tally at 4 of 4 would prove waiting wrong — the bottom confirmed while we stood aside. Conversely, a weekly SPX close below the 200-day (7,325.05) with HY OAS above 4% would prove the correction framing wrong — this becomes a bear episode and the ladder's re-entry rungs are void.

reaction.trapRisk: Friday's bounce was broad and fast — OKLO +23.18%, SMR +15.56%, RKLB +16.48%, VST +10.42% in a single session — while the tape is still -5.96% off its high and SMH sits below Zone 2. A pivot-and-fail here means the bounce retraces into the SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH 580-600 failure zone and rolls over; entries must wait for the failure-zone verdict, not chase the first green day. No position is sized off a single-day bounce, and any probe waits for a close holding above the zone, not an intraday spike.

strategyPosture: Watch, with probe-ready discipline: the correction is real (SPX -5.96% from its high, SMH -30.94%), the mechanical tally is 3 of 4, but zone occupancy is unconfirmed and the VIX at 25.64 is still above the 25 stand-down line, so no new deployment until a fresh Zone 2 print plus a VIX close below 25.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real even if the rollover call is not: a -11.54-point Mag7-vs-SPY gap means index-level calm masks genuine weakness in the names that dominate the index by weight. Credit conditions can flip fast — the rotation read holds only while lending stays loose and HY OAS stays contained. If spreads widen, rotation becomes rollover retroactively.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average -17.44% from their 52-week highs against SPY at -5.9%, an 11.54-point divergence gap (weakest GOOGL -30.3%, strongest AAPL -3.7%). SPX itself is -5.96% from its 120-day high of 7,844.52 and still +0.71% above its 200-day average of 7,325.05. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% on SLOOS, far below the ~40% stress threshold, and high-yield spreads sit at 3.48%, calm.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as an orderly leadership rotation: the index is only modestly off its high while the mega-cap leaders take the hit, and credit is not confirming a broad rollover.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4% or SLOOS tightening toward stress levels would void the rotation read.

themes.counterRead: Multiple compression can outlast good revenue for quarters, and the mechanical tally is 3 of 4 with the missing leg the one that matters: zone occupancy is unconfirmed (SMH below Zone 2, NVDA between zones at $186.64). Buying the fundamentals before the zone confirms is catching a falling multiple. The setup is real; the timing is not yet.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue data runs the other way. NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year while the stock sits -23.3% below its high at $186.64; AVGO revenue is growing 55% with a 67.8% gross margin and 42.1% free-cash-flow margin while -40.7% off its high; LRCX revenue is growing 131.3% year over year while -54.3% off its high. SMH is -30.94% from its high and closed Friday at $463.96, below Zone 2 ($470-505), with volume at 1.53x its 20-day average — a climax signature, not quiet distribution.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure: Fundamentals Ahead of Price
themes.narrative: The market is pricing an AI funding unwind: semis are the weakest leg, SMH is down 23.1% over 20 days, and NVDA's decline is tagged an acute catalyst, not mere sentiment.
themes.watchFor: SMH daily close back inside Zone 2 ($470-505) with VIX closing below 25.

themes.counterRead: A +10% to +23% single-day bounce inside a -20% to -32% monthly drawdown is a relief rally until proven otherwise, and the fastest bounces make the worst chases. Friday's close inside the zone is step one, not a buy signal. The power complex is the most DATA_AHEAD corner of the board, and also the easiest place to get trapped buying the bounce.
themes.dataAnchor: OKLO rose 23.18% Friday, SMR 15.56%, RKLB 16.48% and VST 10.42% — yet the one-month damage is intact: OKLO -31.59%, SMR -31.01%, VST -20.17% over one month, and VST is still -36.6% from its 52-week high at $124.80. The fundamentals behind the bounce are not a story: VST revenue is growing 19.1% year over year, it trades at 2.4x sales, and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. VST's revenue inflection is flagged DETERIORATING, which tempers the case.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power: Violent Bounce, Still Discounted
themes.narrative: Friday was a power-complex snapback: the market decided nuclear got oversold and repriced it in a single session.
themes.watchFor: VST holding above its $124.80 Friday close on the next down day, rather than giving the whole bounce back.

themes.counterRead: Revenue growth is a trailing fact and multiple compression is a forward judgment: if growth decelerates from here, today's 'cheap' is tomorrow's fair value. The near-term verdicts arrive fast — ONTO reports Monday Nov 9 after the close and AMAT Thursday Nov 12 after the close — so the cohort's trough thesis gets tested by prints before it gets tested by price.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG revenue is growing 27.7% year over year with an 80% gross margin at $179.04, -40.5% from its high, RSI 28.3; SNOW revenue +34.3% at $275.88, -28.3% from its high, RSI 33.6; NET revenue +36.4% at $268.75, -27.4% from its high; MDB revenue +28% at $312.83, -33.9% from its high. All four carry a RECOVERY revenue inflection in the conviction ranking, and DDOG (84), SNOW (76) and NET (76) sit at the top of the watchlist promotions.
themes.label: Enterprise Software: Growth Intact at the Trough
themes.narrative: Enterprise software has been derated as if AI disrupts the model itself: the whole cohort sits 27-41% below its highs with oversold momentum readings across the board.
themes.watchFor: ONTO earnings Nov 9 after close and AMAT earnings Nov 12 after close: guidance holds or the trough thesis weakens.

themes.counterRead: The next data point is the one that can change this read: October CPI lands Tuesday Nov 10 at 8:30am, and a hot print reprices the December path the same morning. A 10-year pushing above 4.84% on a hot CPI would turn a headwind into a trigger. Until then, rates argue for patience, not panic.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve is positively sloped (2s10s +0.38), the real 10-year is 2.61%, the policy rate (DFF) is 3.88% and 10-year breakeven inflation is 2.23% — an orderly higher-rate regime, not a disorderly one. Credit agrees: HY OAS 3.48% is calm and below the 4% stand-down line, and the VIX at 25.64 is rolling over from its 28.18 five-day high (-9.01% Friday). Rates are the headwind pressing multiples down, not a credit event breaking the market.
themes.label: Rates and Credit: The Headwind, Not the Trigger
themes.narrative: Rate-cut hopes are fading — matched headlines this week run on a Fed chair warning for AI stocks and fading cut odds — and the long end is pricing higher-for-longer, with the 10-year at 4.84% and the 30-year at 5.25%.
themes.watchFor: October CPI Tuesday Nov 10, 8:30am: a hot print pushing the 10-year above 4.84% reprices the December path.
